patch.objective: Enterprise risk management frameworks and risk treatment strategies

sources.cite: CompTIA SecurityX CAS-005 (V5) exam page: domains Governance, risk, and compliance 20%, Security architecture 27%, Security engineering 31%, Security operations 22%
sources.note: Relevant text: Security architecture covers network architecture ('segmentation, microsegmentation, VPN, always-on VPN, and API integration'), Zero Trust ('defining subject-object relationships'), security boundaries ('asset identification, management, attestation, data perimeters, and secure zones') and deperimeterization ('SASE, SD-WAN, and software-defined networking'); Security operations covers incident response including root cause analysis. The page has no objective text on federation by name. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11; the CAS-005 objectives PDF was not re-read here. The course's unit titles are the course's own wording. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's federation-token-forgery (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

sources.cite: NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29, February 26, 2024), GOVERN function: GV.RM-01, GV.RM-02, GV.RR-02, GV.OV
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of NIST's 'CSF 2.0 Implementation Examples' PDF (dated February 26, 2024), which restates the Core outcomes: GV.RM-02 'Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained'; GV.RR-02 'Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced'; GV.OV 'Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy'. The CSWP 29 document itself was not opened.
